reviews.text:
I had to take Cocoliso, a Fischer's lovebird, to Gwanavver Veterinarian because he was suddenly having trouble breathing. He was making a noise like he was struggling to breathe. I thought he had a cold and expected them to give him antibiotics. When they examined him, they told me he had a seed stuck in his trachea, that he was in very bad shape. He was admitted and they took an X-ray to see where the seed was... unfortunately, it was at the end of his trachea and couldn't be removed. They tried everything with antibiotics, oxygen... and everything else necessary, along with the love and care of the entire team. In the end, it wasn't possible. He passed away fighting and with so much love. Don't hesitate to take your pets to the vet as soon as you hear them making noises while breathing or if they're having trouble breathing.

I want to thank the entire team at Gwana Vet Veterinarians for everything. ❤️
Very bad, my wife ordered a bag of pet food and when we arrived after half an hour they told us there was no time wasted and a lack of professionalism

I called to reserve some special rodent feed for me, and half an hour later when I arrived, they had sold it. Today, being a holiday, I called because I needed eye drops that are artificial tears, and they told me they would sell them to me if I had a consultation with them… THEY ARE INTERESTED IN MONEY, NOT THE HEALTH OF THEIR PATIENTS!

I took my one-year-old hamster, Nene, to the vet because of a blocked eyelid canal. We were seen by Dr. Maria, who was very kind, attentive, and professional. I'm so grateful for all her care of my little guy, her explanations, and her kind recommendations! We hope Nene recovers soon with his treatment, and we'll be back for a checkup! Thank you so much!! 🫶🏻♥️

I have a Syrian hamster that was chewing on the cage bars, and thankfully its mouth is fine. I've been told about the importance of environmental enrichment and the importance of letting it roam freely and cleaning up its play area.
Little information, high prices

My experience leaving my African Grey parrot was wonderful. I left feeling very relaxed and found him adorable, just as playful and affectionate as ever. I really went on my trip with complete peace of mind.

A fantastic experience! My lovebird was very ill because of an egg that wouldn't hatch, and they saved her. She had problems for almost a month as a result, and now, a year after she was admitted, I can say she's perfectly fine! Thank you so much!
I wholeheartedly recommend them for their excellent service and professionalism. They were also incredibly gentle with our lovebirds.
My bunny had an intestinal blockage and he's fine now. I'm so grateful to Gwana, who also gives them medicines they like, which makes it easy to give them.
I highly recommend it because the people are very friendly and professional.

I have a canary with a lot of problems with feather cysts. Luckily, we have specialists in exotic animals who are solving all the problems these feathers are causing.

We are very happy with the service and highly recommend it.

SHAMEFUL.

A few months ago, I took my rabbit to the vet because he had stopped eating. After performing a blood test and an X-ray, for which they charged me nearly €180, they assured me he had a serious problem and that, if left untreated, he would die. They also mentioned a possible liver problem and suggested further tests.

The situation was extremely distressing. I left the clinic convinced my rabbit's days were numbered. However, I decided to take him home and not continue with the tests they suggested.

To this day, my rabbit is perfectly fine. He didn't receive any treatment for that supposed liver problem or for the disease that was supposedly going to kill him, and he continues to live a completely normal life.

I understand that a diagnosis can be complicated and that no one can guarantee a patient's outcome 100%, but precisely for that reason, I consider it very serious to tell an owner that their pet will die if a certain treatment or tests aren't performed, when later reality proves something completely different.

In addition to the significant financial burden, the emotional impact of receiving that prognosis was enormous. My experience has been very negative, and frankly, I lost all confidence in this clinic.
Highly recommended. The service was excellent, both for us and our rabbit. Both the veterinarians and the support staff were very attentive and demonstrated great experience.

Our parakeet arrived very lethargic, and after tests, he was diagnosed with a heart problem. The treatment they recommended has improved him tremendously, and he's back to his old self. He needs regular checkups, but he has a wonderful quality of life. The whole team treated us exceptionally well, with immense kindness.

Our rabbit was incredibly caring. From the very first call, filled with worry, the communication was attentive and clear. We appreciate being informed about everything from the beginning, including prices, so we aren't misled later, and they aren't the most expensive. In the end, she had intestinal paralysis that could have been very serious, and thanks to the speed and professionalism of the service, we were able to pull her through. Impeccable care that saved her life, and I wanted to share that here.

SURPRISED BY SO MANY POSITIVE REVIEWS. TERRIBLE EXPERIENCE.

If you have a guinea pig or any rodent, my recommendation is to look for a center with specific experience in these animals and, above all, one that provides genuine follow-up care from the veterinarians.

During our four visits, we were seen by four different veterinarians, and none of them seemed to know my guinea pig's medical history or what had happened previously. Each time, we had to explain everything from scratch. For me, this lack of continuity of care was one of the biggest problems.

We initially went because she was making a noise when breathing. They told us it was "apparently pneumonia," without being able to confirm it even after seeing the X-ray. However, on three of the four visits, they considered hospitalizing her, even though she was active, eating, and behaving completely normally. They even considered admitting her and sedating her to determine if the noise was coming from her lungs or teeth, telling us, quite literally, "I love guinea pigs, but they're the worst patients because it's so hard to know what's wrong with them." They prescribed a supposed treatment for suspected pneumonia (weird, right?).

Three months later, she made the same noise again. They told us they didn't have an appointment for another six days and that we should go to the emergency room because a guinea pig could deteriorate in 24 hours. So we did (to an empty waiting room, but paying for an emergency appointment at 12:00 AM). Even though they had previously taken several x-rays at the same center without sedation, this time they told us it was essential to anesthetize her. When I asked them to at least try without sedation, they rudely asked if my refusal was for financial reasons. The answer was that they weren't even going to try. So we paid for the appointment and left.

We then went to another center specializing in rabbits and rodents. They reviewed the same x-ray and told us it was very clear it was pneumonia, explaining why and that there seemed to be a relapse that needed treatment. They also explained that guinea pigs are not usually hospitalized except in extremely serious situations, due to their sensitivity to stress and changes. The contrast was enormous.

We also had problems getting the reports: they sometimes took about a week, and they didn't even list the medications administered. When we asked for them, we were told they were on the prescription they had given us, which we no longer had two months later. Finally, they had to write down the treatment on a piece of paper.

But the worst part was the lack of empathy and the way we were treated. Two of the four people who attended to us were, in my opinion, rude, domineering, and very inconsiderate. Even seeing me cry in the consultation room, I felt that their main concern was making sure it was on record that we were taking the animal voluntarily, instead of showing a minimum of empathy.

I can't comment on their financial motives, but I can say that at certain times I felt they were prioritizing tests, sedations, and hospitalizations whose benefit to my guinea pig I didn't quite understand.

After this experience, we completely lost faith in the center and decided to continue his care elsewhere, where the experience has been entirely different.

You should really take a good look at your love for animals. The first thing you always mention is the price. I'm fed up after spending over €1000 since January on neutering my pets, leaving them with you to get them used to eating hay (which was a total rip-off because after a week they were all the same), tests, check-ups, etc. I call you worried about something, and the same old rude person only knows how to tell me the price. Go to hell! I'm calling because I'm worried; I don't give a damn about the money, I just want to know if it was something serious. I'm not coming back; I'm sure there are professionals out there who love their work. Send me the invoices for everything; you have my contact information via WhatsApp.
Excellent care for my lovebird; taking them there was a great decision. Highly recommended—they know a lot about birds!

What is traumatic for our kittens becomes a pleasant experience for them.
Excellent professionals.
Special mention for Cristina, an exceptional veterinarian who cares for our kittens with the utmost care and attention.
After having used other veterinarians, we wouldn't change for anything.
Irene is the one we see when we enter the clinic. Very friendly and attentive.
They advise us on the best and most appropriate services, tailored to our kittens' needs.

Thank you for your care.

We are so grateful for the exceptional care our guinea pig received, and we did too. The vet was wonderful, and the assistants were incredibly attentive. The whole process was quick and they kept us warmly informed every step of the way. Professional and caring.

Excellent service! I took my baby rabbits there a couple of years ago, and they were seen to them incredibly quickly. Now, my mini-loop bellier (Koda) has had a very serious decline, and they treated him incredibly fast and very well. They explained all the treatments to us and gave us all the possible options with great empathy. A big thank you to the whole team, and I especially want to thank the veterinarian, Lucia, who gave us special attention throughout the procedures and in Koda's care.
I'm so happy with the care my hamster Linda received for having otitis and an abscess. Thanks to Dr. Maripi, everything turned out great. My family and I are thrilled!

A few months ago I wrote a review, and yesterday I received a notification that it was deleted. I'm writing it again.

I would never take any animal to this vet again. I took my parakeet because she had an obvious fracture in her leg. From the very beginning, the only solution they offered was to keep her hospitalized, charge me, and scare me by saying that they might have to amputate her leg and that the chances of her ever having a functional leg were nil… but without explaining practically anything about the treatment or showing me any tests.

For more than a week, they kept repeating that "she was lively but wasn't eating" and that's why they couldn't release her; she had to stay hospitalized for a few more days. When I went to see her, her leg was bandaged, cold, numb, and there was no movement in her toes. She wasn't putting weight on it or reacting. Even so, no one explained that this could indicate a serious circulatory problem or warned me about anything.

When I decided to take her out of there, because everything seemed very strange and they were charging me an exorbitant amount, they prescribed four different medications and also told me that her liver was "damaged" by the medication. All the diagnoses were alarming, but they didn't show me any tests, x-rays, or provide any clear explanations. They just wanted me to pay and keep the animal hospitalized.

Days later, I called, worried because her paw was still completely cold, and they tried to send me to the emergency room several times to charge me more. Later, a staff member even told me that when they discharged her, "she was putting weight on her paw and moving her toes," which was absolutely false.

Finally, I went to another veterinarian, and there they showed me real evidence. The new x-ray clearly showed the fracture. The x-rays they sent me from this clinic (gwana) didn't even clearly show the broken bone they had supposedly been treating for weeks.

Furthermore, they tried to overcharge me several times.

At the new vet, they told me that the first thing they should have offered when I took my bird in was immediate surgery instead of bandaging her leg and giving her medication, or telling me that amputation might be necessary.

I'm left with the impression of a lack of transparency, terrible communication, and a treatment focused more on delaying admissions and bills than on properly informing the animal's owner and making money.
I find it unbelievable and appalling. Don't bring your animals here if you love them.

Here are the X-rays from Gwana in the first photo, the X-rays from the new vet the day I picked her up and took her home, and some conversations where they tried to overcharge me. The other attempts were at the clinic.

Honestly, I want my money back because this is grounds for a complaint.

To this day, my parakeet is using her leg as if nothing ever happened. It fits snugly, it didn't end up crooked or hanging down (like they told me at Gwana it would).

Something very fishy is going on here.

My birds had to be seen at a different vet clinic than their usual one, since they now live in Madrid. They were perfectly healthy and had regular checkups with their previous vets.

My partner took them there, and when they were seen, the vet said they were malnourished (which is impossible, since their diet was approved by their previous vets). From there, they suggested hospitalizing one of them and running extremely expensive tests. Then they asked to have the other one checked (who was perfectly fine and normal) and made up some excuse to keep them under observation for days, run more tests, while sending HEALTHY animals home with a lot of medications they DON'T need.

We checked with another vet, and indeed, not only did they not need these medications, but they were harmful to their health. In this whole charade, they charged us over €1,500.

They treat the owners' concerns like a business, and sadly, they don't care about making healthy animals sick. I hope you read this review before bringing your animals here.

The vet was very good, but for some simple diagnostic tests, they wanted to keep my bird hospitalized and didn't have me sign any consent form for administering anesthesia and taking a blood sample, so I assume they did it without putting him to sleep. Because of how dependent my bird is on me, I didn't want to keep him hospitalized, and they verbally accepted and understood my situation. However, they then asked me to sign a voluntary discharge form, which I didn't understand because it wasn't essential; it was just for tests, not for any treatment that needed to be done there, since we're already providing the treatment at home. Then I had to fight with them to get a report for the follow-up care of the vet who has been treating my bird for 10 years. And in the report, they state that I took my bird against his will, even though they understood that he was there. It's a shame that the excellent care my bird received was marred by such conservative and untrue protocols.

Our overall experience was positive. The veterinarian who treated Zazú was exceptional: friendly, careful, clear, and a true professional. She performed a very thorough examination, including blood work, X-rays, and stool analysis, and we felt she was in good hands the entire time. We went there as an emergency because Zazú, a ten-year-old cockatiel with only one eye and very attached to us, was lethargic, weak, and had regurgitated. Before running the tests, we were advised to keep her hospitalized to facilitate the process. Since Zazú doesn't eat when we're not around, we preferred to wait there. The tests were carried out without any problems, and the presumptive diagnosis was bacterial enteritis with protein loss, with a prescription for home treatment (the veterinarian never even considered the possibility of hospitalizing her for treatment).
The only area for improvement was the paperwork. We left with the dosage and frequency of the medications written on envelopes, but without the treatment duration or the diagnosis. When we requested the report and the tests (blood work, x-ray, fecal exam) via WhatsApp, we were told it would take approximately a week. After insisting for quite some time and explaining that we needed it for his regular veterinarian and for travel, we finally received it that same day.
What bothered me most was the excessive secrecy surrounding the paperwork. Upon leaving, they asked us to sign a document related to not admitting him. Before signing, I clarified that I wasn't refusing hospitalization if it was clinically necessary, but rather that we had decided against admitting him solely for the tests. I was assured that the document referred to that.

However, the report later indicated that hospitalization had been recommended to begin treatment and monitor his progress, but that the guardian hadn't authorized it. This doesn't match what we understood during the consultation, where Zazú was released to us and outpatient treatment was prescribed. This discrepancy made me feel somewhat deceived.

I understand that a hospital needs protocols and to protect itself, but the documentation should align with what was explained before signing it. Despite this, my overall impression is positive. The clinic is very well-equipped, and the veterinarian was a fantastic professional. If Zazú needs care again, I wouldn't hesitate to return. Thank you, above all, for taking such good care of him and treating him so well.

Maripi and María are exceptional; they treat you with so much love and care for the animals as if they were their own. Whenever something seems wrong, they encourage you to come as soon as possible to avoid complications, even if it's just something minor. It's also important to come in for anything unusual, as the life of an exotic animal is much more fragile than that of a small dog or cat. Without a doubt, they are our trusted veterinarian!
Blasete arrived very ill just before turning 10 years old, 15 days later here we are, discharged and in perfect condition.
Very good professionals, we always leave our parrot at the daycare while we go on vacation.

We saw signs of pneumonia; he was making noises when he breathed, and even though he was very well-behaved, we decided to bring him in urgently. Thanks to that, everything turned out great! After an x-ray, they prescribed antibiotics. After two weeks with him and a final x-ray to confirm everything was alright, he's in perfect condition! Thank you so much for everything!! As soon as you see any signs in your little ones, bring them in immediately!!!
Beak trimming, explaining the whole process to me, everything was great

I left my tortoise at a kennel for a 15-day holiday trip. When I first inquired, they told me that a consultation would be required a week prior, which would cost extra, and then I would pay for each day of her stay. This seemed reasonable, so we proceeded. She had her check-up on a Thursday, and I dropped her off the following Friday.

When I dropped her off, they told me they had noticed some orange spots and that they needed to rule out any internal issues. I mentioned that she had been eating carrots that morning, in case that was the reason, but they said it could be many things without specifying, and that it could be something internal. They told me that blood tests and an X-ray would be necessary, and that I would also have to pay for the consultation again. Worried that something might be wrong, I agreed, and now it wasn't just the €208 for boarding plus the €25 consultation; now I also had to pay €169 (€89 for the blood tests, €47 for the X-ray, and €33 for the consultation).

I must emphasize that they also made me wait a very long time. On the day I was leaving for vacation, I arrived at 11:00 AM and didn't leave until 2:30 PM. I understand the 1.5-hour wait for the tests, but not the rest. I wouldn't have minded waiting if the service was good, but when it was finally my appointment, she rushed me in without even closing the examination room door. They didn't give me any of the test results (x-ray and blood work). The vet told me my turtle was perfectly fine, that nothing was wrong with her, and that the orange spots could be from "congestion" during the trip—an explanation I didn't understand at all. She showed me the x-ray, saying that she needed a €10 injection for gas, nothing more. Since they were charging me for the appointment, I took the opportunity to ask a few questions about changing my turtle's aquarium and about her diet, but the answers were so quick they practically made me get up. Finally, the vet got up and stood in the doorway, telling me to finish the appointment. The receptionist ended up answering my questions about the aquarium. Furthermore, I suspect the spots are related to the carrot she ate, which she rubbed against, leaving very subtle marks on her skin.

On another note, during her stay, they informed me that the thermos I bought specifically for this purpose (since we had to provide it for her to stay) burned and is unusable. It's completely melted, and it cost me 44 euros, which I've now lost. They told me my tortoise moved it, but I think they should have prevented this by securing it properly, using more water, or providing one from the center instead of making me bring one I can no longer use. But the worst part is that something could have happened to my tortoise, that she could have ended up with a burn. Thankfully, that didn't happen.

I'm very unhappy. They sent me three photos during her stay, which I appreciate, but the first time I went about four days without any communication, and they didn't respond. I had to call twice because they didn't answer. I also called requesting the invoice and test results. They said they would call back, but they never did.

Finally, when we picked her up, they gave us the test results and invoice. Initially, they wanted to send them to us, but given our previous experience with the call, we decided to wait, and they sent everything a while later.

I feel the tests were unnecessary; they alarmed me, and the service wasn't good. I just needed a vacation stay, and the tortoise had already passed her checkup successfully. They could have taken a closer look at those spots; they would have disappeared soon enough.

Seriously, if you're reading this, don't take your pet here.

You'll leave without 400 euros and without a diagnosis…

Pipi has recovered wonderfully. From the first visit, when I was admitted, I wasn't eating and I had lost weight. They ran tests and admitted me, but I came home jumping and singing. At each visit, they explained everything clearly, taught us how to take better care of him, and told us when to come in at the right time.
Thank you for the care.

An exceptional place! They have such a wonderful love and care for the little ones! Olivia was saved thanks to them!

Especially Chema, a veterinarian who worked with great professionalism and was very kind to us throughout the entire process.

Not recommended at all. As another client said, it's all a business. A complete lack of professionalism and sensitivity regarding the death of a patient under follow-up. After several appointments with my little bird, and while still under observation, it sadly passed away last Wednesday. I informed the clinic and asked their veterinarian to call me back. When I didn't receive a call, I called again today, and the veterinarian's response was that she's been very busy this week and doesn't know if she was informed or not. In short, I felt that this woman lacks sensitivity and empathy towards the death of a patient.

Soy is my tortoise; he's been with me for 28 years. I didn't know where to turn, so I came to Gwanavet. They treated him wonderfully. He needed surgery, but today he was finally discharged. I recommend them 100%.

I have 2 rabbits, one of them obese. After today's check-up and thanks to the monitoring we've been doing of their biochemicals, we managed to control their genitals and now it's time to improve their weight.
100% recommended

We found a fledgling sparrow and didn't know what to do, thinking it had a broken wing (it turned out to be fine). Seeing it in an interior courtyard of a building where it gets sun all day worried us. Then we remembered the clinic because we have a friend who brings their exotic animals there. They were wonderful to us (since we were a bit nervous about the poor bird) and treated us with great understanding and kindness. They didn't charge us for the consultation because it was a wild animal. They are excellent professionals and incredibly friendly; you can tell when someone is passionate about what they do.
The service was very friendly and the place was beautiful 💖 …

I truly have nothing but words of gratitude for the people at Gwanavet. I took my rabbit there because of a strange head tilt, and the treatment was outstanding. The issue was serious, and they were incredibly caring and friendly—one of those places where they listen to you and you leave feeling much more at ease. The improvement was incredible, although we have to keep an eye on its progress. They are true professionals.

The veterinary team is very kind and professional. We found a pigeon with a broken wing because it had become entangled in a small piece of string, which was also partially suffocating it. After trying to call several animal rescue centers in the Madrid area who either didn't answer or couldn't treat it, we finally took the pigeon to Gwana for 24-hour emergency treatment. Maripi, the veterinarian in charge, was exceptional with her care, and for four days they called every day to give us updates on the healing process. They removed the string, took x-rays to check for fractures, treated the swelling, massaged the wing, and fed it until it improved. Here you can see the before and after photos/videos... showing how much it improved! Yesterday we released Erling back into the wild in a park near where we found him. He was in good spirits and flew back into the sky. I am very grateful to the Gwana veterinary team for helping him fly again. I could also see, from the other patients who arrived, that they are a trusted center in the community. A team of angels.

A fantastic experience at Gwana Vet. We took our very sick lovebird, and the veterinarian and the entire team were wonderful and incredibly caring. The service was also incredibly fast and efficient, and they explained everything perfectly. We felt very reassured and well-informed. Highly recommended.

Never take your pets to this clinic!!! They want to admit every animal that comes in, no matter what's wrong with them!! And they just happen to have a cardiac arrest on every single one, and then they tell you they resuscitated them!!! Beware, it's a business with no love for animals!!! They told me my pet had a cardiac arrest and needed resuscitation when in eight years with me he'd never had one, and his heart was perfectly healthy, according to his regular annual checkups with his vet!! I went there in an emergency because there were no other clinics and my usual one was closed. To my surprise, they had to admit him; his condition was extremely serious. The next day I went back and they told me he'd suffered a cardiorespiratory arrest and had to be resuscitated. When they told me that, I naturally decided to euthanize my pet because I didn't want him to suffer, and they told me to go ahead. A year later, I spoke with someone who had just left that clinic with a guinea pig. They told her it would die if she took it, threatening her that it would perish. And coincidentally, they told her the same thing: that it had a heart attack and they had resuscitated it! What a coincidence! They must use that tactic very often. Now it makes me think that maybe my pet could have lived, and all because of this business, which is just a business and has no love for animals! It's a shame it was the only clinic I called! If this has happened to you, please post it here. If they told you your pet needed to be admitted, and then when you arrived they told you they had resuscitated them after a cardiac arrest, you can't imagine the pain it causes me to think that my pet's life didn't end, and all for the money they charged me, along with his ashes—who knows if they're even his ashes... When I arrived at the clinic to collect them, they were under the table, on the floor, thrown there like they were just any old object. And he was my pet, my family member, whom I loved for eight years and will never forget... veterinarians???

I took my rabbit in for emergency care. We arrived scared, especially after the diagnosis of liver torsion, but from the very first minute, the kind and empathetic treatment was outstanding. They are true professionals who take care of every detail with immense care for both the animal and the owner. Furthermore, the service is excellent, and the prices are very reasonable for the quality and peace of mind they offer. I recommend Gwana Vet 100%.

I always bring him in for a nail trim and a general check-up.
Dr. Maripi always gives lots of useful information to help us understand our feathered friends ❤️❤️
Oh my god, I don't even want to think about how expensive this clinic has been... if I have to recommend anything about this place, it's that you don't go in so you don't get attacked.

It's a great place for guinea pigs. Since they specialize in exotic animals, they're very experienced in caring for them.
My guinea pig had two ovarian cysts, and they operated on her. She's perfectly fine now, and thanks to them, she's much healthier and has lived longer. We're very happy.

Excellent exotic animal professionals who provide calm and impeccable care when you're worried about your little one. Their extensive experience caring for exotic species is evident. Bizcochito underwent a spaying procedure and has recovered wonderfully. She was running around the very next day... She confirms she will continue visiting the great GWana Vet team and sends a big "cui-cui" :)

Gwana Vet specializes in exotic animals in Madrid. I went on a recommendation and everything was great. My rabbit had chronic ear infections, they operated on her, and she's doing wonderfully. Thank you so much!

They've treated me wonderfully; they're specialists in exotic animals. I'd been to other vets, but they've sorted everything out here. My pet's eyes are improving, and all the staff are very friendly.

We went to a veterinarian specializing in exotic animals, Gwana Vet. They treated our hamster for an eye problem that required surgery, and everything has gone very well. We are very happy; the specialist who operated on him was excellent.
Fantastic service. Both the reception staff and the veterinarian, Lucía, were very attentive, friendly, and professional at all times. Highly recommended.
Pelusa was at Gwana Vet, a vet without exotic animal specialists. We had to operate on her, and everything went very well. She's now fully recovered. The staff were very kind and helpful.
Just wanted to thank you all for the amazing work of this great team. Special thanks to Maripi, Paula, and Ainhoa.

We arrived terrified because our Tulo had just collapsed. After a month and a half in the hospital, I can only express my deepest gratitude for the incredible care, respect, humanity, and professionalism shown to everyone—from Andrea, his veterinarian, to Jael at reception, Paula, and all the other staff. We will always be thankful that he pulled through and will soon be 15 years old. 💜

It's a total money-making scheme.
I have a rabbit that's been to the vet twice in a row. The first time, they told me it was a bacterial infection, and I spent four weeks paying for consultations and tests. When they discharged him, we went back less than a week later. When I called again to make an appointment for the second episode, they wanted me to bring him in through the emergency room... instead of a regular appointment. Can they be any more shameless?
Let me tell you, I left him admitted, had blood work, an X-ray, a test, and all sorts of other tests, one after the other. When they finally discharged him, I had to pay €73 for two bottles of medicine... I left about €400 poorer, and I see they only told me when to give him one of the medications; they didn't say anything about the other four. When I called, they told me I had to go back for a consultation... pay another €34, and then they'd tell me...?

Seriously, they hadn't discharged him? Nobody told me anything about follow-up appointments, and other times I'd been there they prescribed medication and told me when to stop taking it. In short, it's all a racket. It's always one more consultation, one more test after three or four others...because, "Where do you think it is X and tell me?" Why don't you just do that specific test directly, and avoid putting the poor rabbit through three more tests? Oh, right, because otherwise, you wouldn't get paid for them. I really don't recommend it.
We needed to spay our rabbit. Everything went great. You can tell.

I took my Amazon parrot to the emergency vet for respiratory and heart problems. The care was excellent. After running all sorts of tests, including X-rays and blood work, he was hospitalized for four days and given oxygen, antibiotics, and other medications. They called me to pick him up and continue his treatment at home. Now he's doing wonderfully well, thanks to his treatment. I'm very happy with this veterinarian and the whole team. I highly recommend them.

They're going way overboard sending evidence after evidence to squeeze out as much money as possible. They're looking for the most convoluted case possible just to send even more evidence. Stop it already, it doesn't look good.
For surgeries, I honestly don't think there are any better; my eternal gratitude to the Gwana Vet team for the care they gave our guinea pig.

Snoopy is a year old. She had otitis caused by a growth in her ear, which was surgically removed with an electrocautery device, as they specialize in exotic animals. She's perfectly fine after a week, and the service was truly exemplary, and they were very caring as well.

I have two Forpus cats; one of them has a hernia and can't go into heat. Today we had the hormonal implant inserted, and we won't have to worry about it again until next year.

Words cannot express my gratitude to Gwana Vet Hospital and especially to Dr. Maripi Lanzarot for what they did for our rabbit. They placed several internal and external supports to try to save his leg. Today he walks and even runs, living a normal life, practically without any lasting effects. I absolutely do not recommend this clinic. After spending €400, the experience has been disastrous for the following reasons:
Lack of continuity: A different veterinarian saw my pet every day, which led to constant misinformation and serious discrepancies regarding the animal's condition.
Lack of transparency regarding tests: I was not given the report or test results until I repeatedly demanded them. The last time, they even responded very rudely.

It's unbelievable that I have to "beg" for information I've already paid for.
No follow-up: Once my pet was discharged and I received payment, there was absolutely no interest in their progress. They showed no concern whatsoever for their recovery.
Incompetent management: The clinic owner herself called me to ask me to explain the reasons for my complaint, and after hearing everything, she wasn't even able to apologize.
It's a clinic where it seems that only money matters, not animal welfare or respect for the client. If you're looking for a place where they'll treat your pet with genuine care and you with respect, look elsewhere.

Now I understand why there are so many negative reviews, and they all have the same message: high staff turnover + lack of information + worried and confused customers = making money 💸.
I won't be back, and I don't recommend it.
